lines: En ceſt erreur, ladite de Rols ſuppliãt,
Grande fut certeinement l'aſtuce de ce paillard, d'en-
tretenir ladite de Rols, en ceſt erreur trois ans, & dauan
tage. qu'elle infalliblement cuidoit eſtre ſa femme.
mais parce qu'où y a erreur nous diſons qu'il n'y point
de conſentement, ni de volonté {a}: & que melefices ne ſe
commettẽt point ſans propos deliberé, & intention de
malfaire {b} ſingulieremẽt vn adultere, ou autre eſpece de
paillardiſe {c}. ceſte femme ici, comme nous diſcourrons
amplement en lieu propre, meritoit pour raiſon de cet
erreur quelque excuſe. Ce que le Pape Alexãdre iij. ſem
ble auoit formellement deciz & determiné {d} car & les
Papes, & les Empereurs auſſi, en pareils termes excu-
ſent la femme qui ſe remarie: penſant auec pluſieurs au
tres, qui le cuidẽt auſſi, q̃ ſon eſpoux ſoit mort {e} meſme-
mẽt ſi le mari auoit demeuré quatre ans ou plꝰ dehors,
& à la guerre {f}. Excuſe auſſi la vierge, qui epouſe vn hõ
me ia marié, ſi elle penſoit qu'il fuſt à marier {g}. Et le
mary qui trouue ſa belleſœur dans ſon lict, & participe
auec elle, cuidant que ſoit ſa femme eſt, auſſi excuſé {h}.
Et Loth ne fut pas puni d'auoir eu affaire auec ſes deux
filles, leſquelles à la deſrobbée ſ'eſtoiẽt miſes dans ſon
lict: partant qu'il eſtimoit participer auec ſa femme {i}: ni
Iacob auſſi, ſ'approchant de Lea, par ce qu'il cuidoit a-
de ceſte cohabitation ont eſté procreez
deux enfans, l'vn deſquels eſt treſpaſſé.

uncertain.text: de conſentement, ni de volonté {a}: & que melefices ne ſe
uncertain.note: 'melefices' printed with a short-ascender f in an fi ligature, not long ſ; read by the word (malefice). Reading of the vowel 'mele-' (not 'male-') is clear in the image.

uncertain.text: mẽt ſi le mari auoit demeuré quatre ans ou plꝰ dehors,
uncertain.note: 'plꝰ': printed as 'pl' followed by a raised 9-shaped sign (the us/-us abbreviation); transcribed U+A770.

uncertain.text: mary qui trouue ſa belleſœur dans ſon lict, & participe
uncertain.note: 'belleſœur' set with no gap at all; treated as the period compound (belle-sœur) rather than two words 'belle ſœur'. Worth a reconciler check.

uncertain.text: auec elle, cuidant que ſoit ſa femme eſt, auſſi excuſé {h}.
uncertain.note: sic: 'que ſoit ſa femme eſt,' — no 'ce' before 'ſoit' and the comma falls after 'eſt'; verified at high magnification, transcribed as printed.

uncertain.text: filles, leſquelles à la deſrobbée ſ'eſtoiẽt miſes dans ſon
uncertain.note: the mark over the final 'e' of 'ſ'eſtoiẽt' is thin and slanted; read as a tilde (ẽ) rather than an acute, on the sense 's'estoient'. Apostrophe after the long ſ is present.
'paui' as printed; expected sense is 'pluu.' (de aqua pluuia arcenda). Letters p-a-u-i are clear, no l.
the mark after 'D' descends below the baseline and reads as a comma rather than a period; could be a low-set period.

final letter of 'penule' is a round x-height glyph matching the 'e' of the same word, whereas the next line's 'penult.' clearly ends in the curl-topped italic t; so 'penule.' as printed, but the two are the same abbreviation and this may be a worn t.
mark after 'D' reads as a comma (descending tail), as in margin_notes[1]; could be a period.
the glyph between the points is a short serifed stroke, an old-style figure 1 rather than the tall italic capital I used in 'Iuriſdic' and 'Infect'; could be read 'i'/'I'.
minim count: read as xxxiiij (34); xxxiij is possible.
no point visible between 'q' and 'j' here, unlike the 'q. j.' of notes g and h; transcribed as printed.
no point after the opening 'l' (contrast notes a, b, c, e). A paper fibre crosses between 'vxor.' and 'prea'.
'leguee' as printed (l-e-g-u-e-e); the intended reading is presumably 'legatæ' (l. vxor præ-legata), so the fourth letter may be a damaged 'a'.
no point after the opening 'c' (contrast note h 'c. j.').
minim count: read as xxxiij (33); xxxij is possible. No final point after 'j'.
